introduction: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá read his own time as two processes at once: one of breakdown, in war, armaments, racial hatred and the collapse of old loyalties; and one of renewal, quiet and for the most part unseen, that would outlast it. These passages set love against hatred as life against death, describe the war he foresaw and lived through, speak of two calls raised in the world, of a century in the pains of birth, and of opposition that only spreads what it attacks. A hundred voices stand beside them: the prophets on light in darkness and on tearing and healing, the Gospels and Paul, the Qur’an, and writers who watched the same age, among them Tennyson, Arnold, Hugo, Kipling, Du Bois, Owen and Yeats, some of whom saw only the breaking.
questions: "Love is the cause of life, and hatred spells death or disintegration." Heraclitus said that strife is the father of all things. What truth is there in each?
Yeats saw the centre failing and asked what rough beast was being born; this talk sees a century in labour with a new world. What makes the difference in what an upheaval brings forth?
Several passages find a hidden wisdom in calamity. How does the warning of Jesus about the tower in Siloam limit what may be said?
Opposition is said to raise the fame of the Cause, as Tertullian said of persecution. When does opposition strengthen a movement, and when does it not?
Two calls are said to be raised in the world. How do you tell them apart in practice?
"Growth only comes by working for others." How would you test that against your own experience?

outside.why: The first letter of John says that whoever does not love remains in death, and that love is the passage from death to life.
Heraclitus held that war is the father of all things and that strife brings everything about. What does this talk see that he did not, and what did he see?
Jeremiah was sent both to root out and pull down and to build and plant. Here those two works are divided between "those around us" and "we." Does every renewal also pull something down?
The Preacher describes the dissolving of a life: the dust returns to the earth as it was.
Jesus says that a grain of wheat remains alone unless it falls into the ground and dies.
Paul says that what is sown is not brought to life unless it dies.
Zechariah heard that it is not by might, nor by power, but by the Spirit.
Paul asks that evil be overcome with good, which is to answer the thought of hate with the thought of love.
Isaiah foresees the wolf dwelling with the lamb, and none hurting or destroying.
Jesus warns that the kingdom will be taken from those who do not bear its fruits and given to others.
Du Bois opened his book in 1903 by saying that the problem of the twentieth century is the problem of the colour line.
Lincoln warned in 1858 that a house divided against itself cannot stand.
Jesus speaks of wars and rumours of wars, nation rising against nation.
Eisenhower said that every gun made and warship launched is a theft from those who hunger and are not fed.
The letter of James asks where wars come from, and answers: from desires that war within.
Jesus says that all who take the sword shall perish with the sword.
Kipling warned an empire at the height of its power that its pomp might be one with Nineveh and Tyre.
Yeats wrote in 1916 that too long a sacrifice can make a stone of the heart.
Wilfred Owen, who died in that war, called the praise of dying for one's country the old lie.
Lincoln observed of his own war that both sides read the same Bible and prayed to the same God against each other.
Isaiah looks to a day when nations beat their swords into ploughshares and learn war no more.
Hobbes thought both sayings true: that man is a god to man, and that man is a wolf to man.
Huxley held that ethical progress depends on combating the struggle that nature sets going.
Tennyson saw nature red in tooth and claw shrieking against the creed of love.
The Qur’an says: truth has come and falsehood has vanished, for falsehood is bound to vanish.
Arnold heard the sea of faith withdrawing and saw ignorant armies clashing by night. On what does this passage rest its certainty that spirituality will prevail?
John's Gospel says that the light shines in darkness, and the darkness has not overcome it.
Paul quotes an early hymn: awake, thou that sleepest, and arise from the dead.
Paul says that the night is far spent and the day is at hand, and asks for the armour of light.
Yeats wrote after the war that the best lack all conviction while the worst are full of passionate intensity.
John's Gospel says that people loved darkness because their deeds were evil, and that whoever does evil hates the light.
Yeats saw things falling apart, the centre failing, and a blood-dimmed tide loosed on the world.
Moses sets life and death before his people and tells them to choose life.
Jesus speaks of two gates and two ways, one broad and one narrow.
Elijah asks the people how long they will waver between two opinions.
Jesus says that he came not to send peace on earth, but a sword.
Simeon says of the child Jesus that he is set for the fall and rising again of many.
Jesus says that he came to cast fire on the earth, and wishes it were already kindled.
Haggai hears that heaven and earth and all nations will be shaken, and that the desire of all nations will come.
The Revelation of John hears from the throne: behold, I make all things new.
A psalm says that God is a refuge though the earth be removed and the mountains carried into the sea.
Paul speaks of a trumpet at which the dead are raised and all are changed in a moment.
Jesus says of his hearers that seeing they do not see, and hearing they do not hear.
Isaiah has God say: I form the light and create darkness; I make peace and create evil. How does that hard saying compare with perceiving wisdom through the forces of mischief?
Isaiah says that darkness covers the earth, and that over it a light is rising.
Pope concluded that whatever is, is right. This passage quotes a like saying, "nothing in creation is more perfect than what is," and adds "in one sense." What does the qualification guard against?
Mary sings of the mighty put down from their seats and the humble exalted.
Jesus says that many who are first shall be last, and the last first.
Paul says that there is neither Jew nor Greek, bond nor free, for all are one.
This is the saying of Jesus about the abomination of desolation that the talk interprets.
Hosea says: he has torn, and he will heal us; he has struck, and he will bind us up.
Joseph tells his brothers that what they meant for evil God meant for good.
Jesus refused to read a disaster as a judgment on those it killed. What may be said about the wisdom of a calamity, and what may not?
Shelley calls the autumn wind destroyer and preserver in one, driving dead leaves and carrying seeds.
Shelley ends his ode: if winter comes, can spring be far behind?
Paul hears the whole creation groaning together in the pains of birth until now.
Yeats also saw his century in labour, and asked what rough beast was slouching toward Bethlehem to be born. What decides what a time of upheaval gives birth to?
Tennyson's dying king says that the old order changes, yielding place to new, and that God fulfils himself in many ways.
Marx and Engels wrote that in their age all that is solid melts into air. They looked to a new society from that melting; what does this talk look to?
Shakespeare's Jaques says that all the world is a stage, and all the men and women players.
A psalm promises that a thousand may fall at one's side and it shall not come near.
The Song of Songs says that many waters cannot quench love, nor floods drown it.
Gamaliel advised the council to leave the new teaching alone, since opposition could not overthrow what was of God.
Tertullian told the persecutors of his day that the more Christians were mown down the more they grew.
Paul says that what happened to him has turned out for the advance of his message.
The Qur’an says of those who plotted against the Prophet: they plot, and God plots, and God is the best of plotters.
The Qur’an says that they would put out the light of God with their mouths, and that God will perfect his light.
Jesus charges the religious leaders of his day with shutting the kingdom against others and not entering themselves.
Jesus tells his disciples not to fear those who can kill the body.
A psalm says not to put trust in princes, whose breath goes out and whose plans perish.
Isaiah says that God brings princes to nothing; scarcely are they planted when they wither.
Paul says that the struggle is not against flesh and blood but against the rulers of the darkness of this world.
Gibbon tells how a humble religion outlived the empire that persecuted it.
Mark tells of Herod, who feared John, had him killed, and is remembered for it.
Shelley's conqueror, the king of kings, is now a broken statue in an empty desert.
Daniel foretells a kingdom set up by the God of heaven that shall never be destroyed.
Machiavelli observed that armed prophets conquer and unarmed ones come to ruin. How does the comparison of Napoleon and Christ answer him?
Jesus says on the night of his arrest: be of good cheer; I have overcome the world.
The first letter of John says that the victory that overcomes the world is faith.
Jesus compares the Spirit to the wind, which blows where it wills and is known only by its sound.
Isaiah says that the people who walked in darkness have seen a great light.
Genesis begins with darkness on the face of the deep, and the word: let there be light.
A psalm says that weeping may endure for a night, but joy comes in the morning.
The Qur’an says that God brings those who believe out of darkness into light.
The Qur’an calls God the light of the heavens and the earth.
Plato pictures humanity as prisoners in a cave who take shadows for the truth until they are turned to the light.
Kant called enlightenment the release from self-incurred tutelage through the courage to use one's own reason. What dispels dogma in this passage, and is it the same thing?
Emerson asked why his age should grope among the dry bones of the past when the sun shines today also.
Habakkuk foresees the earth filled with the knowledge of the glory of God.
Kipling's ballad begins by saying that East is East and West is West and never the twain shall meet, and then tells of two men who did. What is being said here about East and West?
Tennyson asks the bells to ring out the feud of rich and poor and ring in the thousand years of peace.
Jeremiah says of false healers that they treat the wound lightly, saying peace, peace, when there is no peace.
Elijah heard, after wind and earthquake and fire, a still small voice.
Paul quotes the prophet: how beautiful are the feet of those who bring good tidings of peace.
Paul asks his readers to put away anger and clamour and be kind to one another.
Tennyson's Ulysses says how dull it is to pause, to make an end, to rust unburnished.
Jesus says that whoever would save his life shall lose it, and whoever loses it shall save it.
Thoreau went to the woods alone to learn what life had to teach. Is there really no growth that begins with the self?
Victor Hugo told a congress in 1849 that a day would come when war between the nations of Europe would seem absurd.
Isaiah speaks of a house that shall be called a house of prayer for all people.

john-epistle-abideth-in-death.text: We know that we have passed from death unto life, because we love the brethren. He that loveth not his brother abideth in death

john-hateth-the-light.text: And this is the condemnation, that light is come into the world, and men loved darkness rather than light, because their deeds were evil. For every one that doeth evil hateth the light, neither cometh to the light, lest his deeds should be reproved. But he that doeth truth cometh to the light, that his deeds may be made manifest, that they are wrought in God

ephesians-rulers-of-the-darkness.text: For we wrestle not against flesh and blood, but against principalities, against powers, against the rulers of the darkness of this world, against spiritual wickedness in high places

romans-night-is-far-spent.text: The night is far spent, the day is at hand: let us therefore cast off the works of darkness, and let us put on the armour of light

john-light-shineth-in-darkness.text: And the light shineth in darkness; and the darkness comprehended it not

haggai-shake-all-nations.text: For thus saith the Lord of hosts; Yet once, it is a little while, and I will shake the heavens, and the earth, and the sea, and the dry land; And I will shake all nations, and the desire of all nations shall come: and I will fill this house with glory

matthew-not-peace-but-a-sword.text: Think not that I am come to send peace on earth: I came not to send peace, but a sword

luke-fall-and-rising-again.text: And Simeon blessed them, and said unto Mary his mother, Behold, this child is set for the fall and rising again of many in Israel; and for a sign which shall be spoken against; (Yea, a sword shall pierce through thy own soul also,) that the thoughts of many hearts may be revealed

jeremiah-to-root-out-and-to-plant.text: See, I have this day set thee over the nations and over the kingdoms, to root out, and to pull down, and to destroy, and to throw down, to build, and to plant

matthew-take-the-sword.text: Then said Jesus unto him, Put up again thy sword into his place: for all they that take the sword shall perish with the sword

mark-save-his-life-shall-lose-it.text: For whosoever will save his life shall lose it; but whosoever shall lose his life for my sake and the gospel's, the same shall save it

john-epistle-overcometh-the-world.text: For whatsoever is born of God overcometh the world: and this is the victory that overcometh the world, even our faith

matthew-first-shall-be-last.text: But many that are first shall be last; and the last shall be first

isaiah-house-of-prayer-for-all.text: Even them will I bring to my holy mountain, and make them joyful in my house of prayer: their burnt offerings and their sacrifices shall be accepted upon mine altar; for mine house shall be called an house of prayer for all people

peter-new-heavens-and-a-new-earth.text: Looking for and hasting unto the coming of the day of God, wherein the heavens being on fire shall be dissolved, and the elements shall melt with fervent heat? Nevertheless we, according to his promise, look for new heavens and a new earth, wherein dwelleth righteousness

hosea-torn-and-he-will-heal.text: Come, and let us return unto the Lord: for he hath torn, and he will heal us; he hath smitten, and he will bind us up. After two days will he revive us: in the third day he will raise us up, and we shall live in his sight

quran-truth-hath-come.text: And say: Truth hath come and falsehood hath vanished away. Lo! falsehood is ever bound to vanish.

quran-out-of-darkness-into-light.text: Allah is the Protecting Guardian of those who believe. He bringeth them out of darkness into light. As for those who disbelieve, their patrons are false deities. They bring them out of light into darkness. Such are rightful owners of the Fire. They will abide therein.

quran-they-plot-and-allah-plots.text: And when those who disbelieve plot against thee (O Muhammad) to wound thee fatally, or to kill thee or to drive thee forth; they plot, but Allah (also) plotteth; and Allah is the best of plotters.

shelley-destroyer-and-preserver.text: Wild Spirit, which art moving everywhere; / Destroyer and preserver; hear, oh, hear
shelley-destroyer-and-preserver.author: Percy Bysshe Shelley

shelley-if-winter-comes.text: The trumpet of a prophecy! O, Wind, / If Winter comes, can Spring be far behind
shelley-if-winter-comes.author: Percy Bysshe Shelley

owen-the-old-lie.text: My friend, you would not tell with such high zest / To children ardent for some desperate glory, / The old Lie: Dulce et decorum est / Pro patria mori
owen-the-old-lie.author: Wilfred Owen

dubois-color-line.text: the problem of the Twentieth Century is the problem of the color-line
dubois-color-line.author: W. E. B. Du Bois
